description: Bank of daily missions — every mission happens off-screen, and its estimated time is never less than five times the card's minutes (the card is three minutes, so the floor is fifteen).

missions.instruction_ar: Make a simple dish with one of your parents supervising — a salad or a sandwich — and clean up your space afterwards.
Plan to buy three items with a set amount of money: write the list, compare the prices, and check the change.
Write a short letter to a grandparent, an uncle or an aunt, and hand it over or send it.
Choose one change in your room and carry it out from start to finish: sort the books, or rearrange the desk.
Teach a younger brother or sister, or a neighbour's child, something you are good at — tying shoelaces, or a maths problem.
Go outside and write down five observations about what you saw: weather, birds, plants — then draw one of them.

missions.title_ar: I Fix, I Don't Throw Away
missions.instruction_ar: Find something simple that is broken in the house and try to fix it with your parents supervising.
Read a chapter of a paper book, then summarise it in three sentences for someone in your family.
Gather clothes or toys you no longer use, and get them ready to give away in charity.
Draw a simple map from memory of the way from your home to the nearest mosque or park, then check it.
Ask a grandfather or grandmother about a memory from their childhood, listen without interrupting, then tell it to your family.
Write tomorrow's plan in five points, and in the evening tick off what you got done.

residual_low.why: Arabic specifies a grandfather, paternal uncle, or maternal aunt; English broadens to grandparent/uncle/aunt and loses the specific kinship terms.
Arabic says 'a younger brother' (أخًا أصغر), not 'brother or sister'; 'sister' is added.
Arabic 'فأفدت' means 'and I benefited/gave benefit', not specifically 'shared'; the English shifts the emphasis.
The Arabic says 'a younger brother' (أخًا أصغر); 'or sister' is added in English.
